Subject: Sudden drop in throughput + p99 tails impacting checkout

Team —

We started seeing a steady drop in checkout throughput on Saturday morning UTC and a large increase in p99 tail latency and 5xx errors for our busiest region (us-west). Impact: failed completions for ~4% of requests at peak and overall throughput down ~18% on our production workload. This is affecting a subset of high-concurrency customers — checkout pages are timing out and retry storms are kicking in.

Quick facts from our side:
- Window: 2027-11-13 02:00–06:00 UTC
- p50/p95/p99 before: 30/120/420 ms; during: 40/280/3200 ms
- Error type: gRPC 13 / internal_completion_timeout and occasional 500s
- We attached a cropped trace and request-level CSV from our logs for your engineers. (attached: novaco_sla_logs_20271114.csv)

Can we get this triaged ASAP? We have Black Friday prep next week and need guaranteed throughput. We will make senior ops/exec available for a call.

—Lina
Lina Gomez
Head of Infrastructure, Novaco Retail

Subject: Re: Sudden drop in throughput + p99 tails impacting checkout

Folks — short technical readout from the War Room run (10:00 PT). Key observations:

1) Queueing/backpressure signature: we see sustained queue depth on the front-end workers when Novaco traffic peaks. The serving runtime reports a sharp increase in in-flight KV cache misses and a correlated spike in kernel latency for attention steps.
2) Concurrency cap interactions: Novaco's production traffic pattern includes bursts of many short-lived conversations; our adaptive concurrency cap hit hard limits on some worker groups which caused local request queuing and then spillback.
3) Error pattern: internal_completion_timeout triggered when requests waited > 2.5s in the local worker queue before execution. A small portion (0.6%) converted to 500s when the runtime rejected at the RPC layer.

Proposed mitigation plan (ordered by rollback safety):
A) Immediate (10–20m): increase per-customer concurrency cap for Novaco by 2x on the busiest shards and enable per-customer soft-queue spillover to spare workers. Expected: drop p99 by ~30–50% on initial tests. Risk: small cost increase.
B) Short term (1–3h): promote Novaco to an isolated Dedicated pool and re-route traffic. This removes cross-customer interference and gives us headroom. Rolling the pool should be safe — we will do canary, monitor for error regressions.
C) Medium term (24–72h): root-cause deeper KV-cache miss pattern — instrument sequence-length distribution and kernel selection heuristics; consider a micro-quantization path for Novaco's common model variant.

I'll open a mitigation runbook ticket and push the immediate cap increase now. Marissa — if you want exec-level notes we can include expected cost delta for the temporary Dedicated pool commitment.
